entries.title: The quiet pond
entries.hint: Somewhere in the start parish the smallest pond keeps a secret.
entries.reveal: Small ponds warm quickly in spring, and sunfish often nest in their shallows - state wildlife agency pond guides say to look for round, fanned-out nest beds.

entries.title: The Bay pond
entries.hint: The smallest pond in the Bay start county hides a quiet spot.
entries.reveal: Many Bay Area ponds and reservoirs hold introduced sunfish and bass; state wildlife agency pages explain which waters are open to fishing.

entries.title: The high lake shore
entries.hint: The mountain world hides one quiet shore spot far from the centre.
entries.reveal: Cold mountain water holds more dissolved oxygen, which is one reason trout do well there (general state wildlife agency guidance).

entries.title: The far lakeshore
entries.hint: The forest world hides one quiet shore spot far from the centre.
entries.reveal: Shade from shoreline trees keeps lake edges cooler, and fallen wood gives small fish cover - a general point in state wildlife agency habitat guides.

entries.title: The canyon eddy
entries.hint: The canyon world hides one quiet shore spot far from the centre.
entries.reveal: In a river, fish often rest in slower water behind rocks and bends and wait for food to drift past - general state wildlife agency angling guidance.

entries.title: The marsh cut
entries.hint: The delta world hides one quiet shore spot far from the centre.
entries.reveal: Marsh edges are nurseries: young fish, shrimp and crabs shelter among the grasses - a general point in state wildlife agency coastal guides.

entries.title: Land a largemouth bass
entries.hint: Try a lure at dawn or dusk on a bayou or lake.
entries.reveal: Largemouth bass are ambush feeders around cover; state wildlife agency guides suggest wet hands and a quick release.

entries.title: Land a red drum
entries.hint: Marsh water and a lake, shrimp or cut bait.
entries.reveal: Red drum usually carry one or more dark tail spots; size and limit rules come from the state wildlife agency.

entries.title: Run a crawfish trap line
entries.hint: Set a trap on a canal or pond in the cool months, then come back and check it.
entries.reveal: Louisiana crawfish are often raised in flooded rice fields after harvest; real trapping follows state wildlife agency rules.

entries.title: Gulf slam
entries.hint: Bass, redfish and a crawfish haul in the parish world.
entries.reveal: Different species need different water, bait and time of day - matching them is what anglers learn from state wildlife agency fishing guides.

entries.title: Land a striped bass
entries.hint: Cast from the Bay shore at dawn or dusk.
entries.reveal: Striped bass move between salt and fresh water; licences and rules come from the California state wildlife agency.

entries.title: Pull up a Dungeness crab
entries.hint: A crab line on the Bay shore in the cooler months.
entries.reveal: Real crabbing has size, sex and season rules set by the state wildlife agency - the game only records a play tag.

entries.title: Land a rainbow trout
entries.hint: A fly rod on the lake shore, dawn or dusk.
entries.reveal: Trout need cool, clean, oxygen-rich water; state wildlife agency guides recommend barbless hooks for release.
